items.title: Pedestrian directions at roundabout
items.body:
### Description
The pedestrian directions for a roundabout count both on- and off-roads for a roundabout.

At the following roundabout I was walking on the east side of Broerdijk from north to south. The voice instructed me to take the 5th exit on the roundabout. Clearly there are only 4 exits.
I believe it counted it as follows:
 - current: Broerdijk north off-road
 - 1st exit: Broerdijk north on-road
 - 2nd exit: Hengstdalseweg west off-road
 - 3rd exit: Hengstdalseweg west on-road
 - 4th exit: Broerdijk south off-road
 - 5th exit: Broerdijk south on-road
https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=19/51.83359/5.88561

### How to reproduce?
Find walking directions from eg Broerdijk 47 to Broerdijk 91
Look at the detailed instructions and see: Roundabout: take 5 exit and go Broerdijk

### Your Environment
OsmAnd Version: 4.1.11
Android/iOS version: Android 11
Device model: Oneplus Nord

**Maps used (online or offline):**   
If you have an issue related to offline maps, tell us the exact name of the map file where the issue occurs and its edition date.

items.title: Turn lanes are incorrect for bicycle / pedestrian (as it's non driving profile)
items.body:
### Problem

take the bike route https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=graphhopper_bicycle&route=52.399331%2C13.454494%3B52.398910%2C13.452437#map=17/52.399182/13.454170

osmand will give the instructions "turn slightly right" and "after 7 meters turn left".
this makes no sense at all; there is no "slight right turn" there, only a junction with a non-straight angle and sideways.

### Solution

the general solution would be "low-pass filtering" the route, reducing the granularity to something that actually makes sense for the particular mode of transportation. the challenge is doing that without violating physical constraints.

items.title: Feature request: better pedestrian routing, configurable routing

labels.name: Nice to Have
labels.description: Should be fixed but there is no priority or no possibility to fix it within current horizon planning

items.body:
Hi,

I'm quite new to osmand, using ~.  I'm using the pedistrian profile, the osmand maps and the internal routing algorithm.

I experience that routing often prefers streets over paths if using streets leads to a slightly smaller distance.  It navigates me over streets where I never saw anybody walking because it would be deadly.  Similarly, I don't want to use any streets when cycling because it is often really dangerous.

I want to suggest to, at least, allow some fine tuning to control the routing algorithm.  I would like to forbid using streets.  It would also be very nice if I could adopt weights/costs on the fly by myself.

Alternatively, you could maybe add a "hiking" routing profile.  That could e.g. prefer a route though woods over a slightly shorter route on asphalt under the burning sun.

But my main and most important point is: let me (optionally) disallow streets for pedetrian and cycling.  Can be a life saver.

TIA,

Michael.

items.title: Search cannot find highway=pedestrian as a multipolygon

labels.name: Nice to Have

items.body:
### Description

Searching on a street name. If a street is defined as a multipolygon but no `place=square` tag, it cannot be searched.

### Steps to reproduce

Download Standard Map for Belgium (Oct 1, 2024)

Center the map on Brussels (50.8523 4.3495)

Search this: Marché aux Poissons - Vismarkt

### Actual result

The search returns a list of places in other cities. No relevant search results nearby.

### Expected result

Return the following multipolygon: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1629615
It has `highway=pedestrian` and `name=Marché aux Poissons - Vismarkt`

We expect it would work like a search for the following place: Place du Jardin aux Fleurs - Bloemenhofplein
That search works fine and returns the following multipolygon: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14039252
It has `highway=pedestrian` and `name=Place du Jardin aux Fleurs - Bloemenhofplein` and `place=square`

The difference is `place=square` but we feel there should not be a reason to index one object and not the other.

### Your Environment (required)

```
Version  OsmAnd~ 4.3.8
10.05.2023 9:31:35
Apk Version : 4.3.8 4308
```

labels.name: Observed
labels.description: Needs more clarification, feedback, or research

items.body:
### Routing engine

- [X] OsmAnd's in-app offline routing
- [X] Any online routing provider (YOURS, openrouteservice, OSRM, etc.)

### Routing Profile

Osmand default pedestrian profile

### Start and end points

Start=43.286500,6.133614
End=43.284459,6.136816

### Actual route

When navigating between this two points with a pedestrian profile, Osmand offline routing makes you cross a primary road which is both dangerous and not ideal (there's a pedestrian underpass with just a small detour). 
I've checked the OSM data and there's no pedestrian crossings at this intersection. There is no signalisation saying pedestrians are not allowed.
https://test.osmand.net/map/navigate/?start=43.286500,6.133614&end=43.284459,6.136816&profile=pedestrian#18/43.28562/6.13466

With the same parameters, OSRM yields a safer and better itinerary, using the pedestrian underpass:
https://map.project-osrm.org/?z=18&center=43.285447%2C6.135682&loc=43.286383%2C6.133767&loc=43.284442%2C6.136867&hl=en&alt=0&srv=2

Wouldn't it be better to increase the penalty of using primary roads to provide safer itineraries? Currently, other than creating a custom routing profile, there doesn't seem to be a way to discourages Osmand from using them.

items.title: Hump and pedestrian crossing being warned too early

labels.name: Observed
labels.description: Needs more clarification, feedback, or research

items.body:
OsmAnd 3.2.3 Unlimited, Android

OsmAnd warns of bumps, humps and pedestrian crossings about 1-2 minutes ahead.

Example:
![Screenshot_2019-03-28-20-55-29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4673289/55691906-382e8b00-5979-11e9-88cb-f532e5624d1c.png)
https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_car&route=-23.06799%2C-47.85648%3B-23.06395%2C-47.85138

If there are bumps/humps near to each other like 500 m, the warning gets "stuck" on the screen and ignores other intermediary obstacles. It should leave the screen after passing the obstacle and reaper when it's close enough to the next obstacle.

I also noticed that OsmAnd warns of pedestrian crossings which are near the road I'm driving on even though they are not part of it (e.g. nearby sidewalk or cross street).

Example:
![Screenshot_2019-03-28-20-58-52](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4673289/55692350-90678c00-597d-11e9-9285-e7313b8dec69.png)
https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_car&route=-23.05886%2C-47.84475%3B-23.05690%2C-47.84216

I suspect that OsmAnd detects and warns about an obstacle if the current way has a node with obstacle tags even far away. It would be better that the warning showed up to 10-15 seconds before the obstacle, otherwise you would simply dismiss the feature.

Map region: Brazil_sao-paulo_southamerica, February 28th. No edit on the area so far.

items.title: add completed/remaining steps widget/navigation in pedestrian mode

labels.name: Nice to Have
labels.description: Should be fixed but there is no priority or no possibility to fix it within current horizon planning

items.body:
### Describe the idea (required) When navigating in the "pedestrian" mode, add custom settings in the form of the number of taken/remaining steps taken on the **widget** and displaying the information on the **graph**. Many fancy gadgets have been doing this for a long time, and some people sense distance in steps better than SI. In addition, when each step is difficult (injury, fatigue, long journey), the pedometer metric becomes more preferable.
### Tell us about the expected behaviour (required) Also make it possible to customize the stride length (0.6m - 0.9m) in the navigation menu, where other parameters, such as average speed, are adjusted. ### Tell us about alternatives you've considered (required) Yandex maps in the latest versions have already added such functionality, ahead of OsmAnd, seizing the initiative.
### Context (optional) This innovation, in theory, will make OsmAnd more popular among tourists and active people. In any case, the trend of pedometers has long been set, trackers are introducing functionality and OsmAnd cannot stand aside, because it is the most touristy.

# 🚀 feature request

### Description

Motorways often visually obstruct cycle paths, making them more difficult to identify. This issue is especially bad when using UniRS—the map style that's supposed to highlight bicycle features—as motorways are drawn with similar colors to those used for local bike routes: 
![signal-2021-03-05-131057](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46303203/110155871-44653200-7db4-11eb-8421-61dc8322ed21.png)




### Describe the solution you'd like

<!-- ✍️--> If you have a solution in mind, please describe it.

This issue could be alleviated with the option to hide motorways and other roads not routeable for bikes.

### Describe alternatives you've considered 

[The CyclOSM tile layer](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/CyclOSM), which is intended for use by cyclists, renders highways with muted colors. [If a new map style were created that used a similar color scheme,](https://www.cyclosm.org/legend.html) that would actually be my preferred solution.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46303203/110156305-c9504b80-7db4-11eb-8a76-e112b3bfbfc0.png)
